---
title: The commands
description: Each command of smalldocs, with its options.
order: 9
---

Each command takes the folder of the project, which holds `_smalldocs.yml` or `_quarto.yml`. If you give no folder, the
command uses the folder you are in.

## render

```bash
smalldocs render [DIR] [--quiet] [--strict]
```

The command builds the site. With `--quiet`, it prints only warnings and errors. With `--strict`, a
warning makes the exit code 1. A broken link and an option that smalldocs ignores are warnings.

## preview

```bash
smalldocs preview [DIR] [--port 4200] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--no-browser]
```

The command builds the site, serves it and opens a browser. When a file of the project changes, it
builds the site again, and the browser loads the new pages. If a build fails, the command prints the
error and keeps the last good site. It listens on this computer only. To listen on other addresses, give `--host`.

## check

```bash
smalldocs check [DIR]
```

The command builds the site into a temporary folder, and keeps your output folder as it is. It still
writes the API pages and runs the `pre-render` and `post-render` commands, as a build does. Then it
lists what to fix:

- the options that smalldocs ignores
- the broken links
- the Markdown that smalldocs does not read or does not run, with the file and the line of each. Examples
  are citations, cross-references, grid tables and code cells

If it finds anything, the exit code is 1.

## api

```bash
smalldocs api build|check|list [--dir DIR]
smalldocs api module NAME [--dir DIR]
```

The command makes the reference pages, checks the docments, lists the documented names, or prints one module as
Markdown. See [The API reference](api.qmd).

## publish

```bash
smalldocs publish gh-pages [DIR] [--branch gh-pages] [--remote origin] [--no-render] [-m MESSAGE]
```

The command builds the site and pushes it to the branch. It works in a temporary worktree, so your
files and your current branch do not change. Your git hooks do not run for the commit of the site.

The command refuses some branches, because they hold your source files:

- your current branch
- the default branch of the remote
- `main` and `master`
- a branch that shares history with your code and holds no site

With `--no-render`, the command publishes the output folder as it is.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Done, with something to fix: `--strict` with warnings, or `check` and `api check` with findings |
| 2 | Stopped: no `_smalldocs.yml` or `_quarto.yml`, a bad option, a failed script, or a port in use |
